Do you have an example of how these changes might look on one of these repos?  It's not clear to me how this would be used correctly except as a way to enforce PDI on repos that don't use it.  For PDI enabled repos, they don't need access to this, right?

> Do you have an example 

The testcase has an example ((debug) log message).

Another case would be retrofitting PDI onto existing boost asio reactors, without re-writing a bunch of stuff.

Basically staying within what's possible to do with 'Inspection only'.

> For PDI enabled repos, they don't need access to this, right?

Probably not, but i don't want to force a single way to use PDI onto people...

Folks should probably use the conversion functions, but i see PDI also as a way of exposing information about D-Bus interfaces to other code, which includes the representations of enum values on D-Bus.

Maybe someone will find a creative use for them, otherwise i can use these to retrofit existing code. Maybe at some point it will be obsolete to expose them.

> The testcase has an example ((debug) log message).

I meant a real example in a repository that would potentially use this.  I did see the test case.  I really don't understand where this fits in the middle between "Use PDI" and "Use strings".  This seems like a medium that's worse than either of those two and we'd probably direct people to use one or the other in that case.

> Maybe someone will find a creative use for them

Would like to see some of these creative uses before we deem this to be a good idea.  sdbusplus is a limited API on purpose.

>  This seems like a medium that's worse than either of those two and we'd
 probably direct people to use one or the other in that case.

You did not outline why this is worse and making blanket statement.

> Would like to see some of these creative uses before we deem this to be a good idea.  sdbusplus is a limited API on purpose.

I have outlined that this is a way to improve the failure mode of exsiting code (failing to build vs. failing at runtime on missing enum member / typo) while making a change that's simple enough to get merged without requiring manual testing.

If you want to require folks migrating code to fully convert it to PDI without intermediate steps you will have to accept that some code will simply not get improved / refactored at all since testing might not be possible.

> sdbusplus is a limited API on purpose.

Overall `sdbusplus` is a mixed API which provides different abstraction layers for the same purpose of D-Bus access.

If you like a restricted API which does everything for you, you should start using PDI.

If you accept the risk of things falling apart (or work on stuff that's well maintained), hardcoding strings can be a way to do it.

If you want to ensure that some enum member you are comparing actually exists, this patch can help with that.

Keep in mind i am sometimes migrating various older / legacy codes to use more modern APIs such as generated headers.

As part of that process i sometimes find property names, method names and other stuff which simply do not exist.

This API i am proposing here is not primarily intended to be used for new code.

It's to patch up existing code and make sure it fails to build when the time comes and the things that (largely unmaintained) code depends on change or disappear.

> You did not outline why this is worse and making blanket statement.

Because you have taken a dependency on PDI, and therefore all the negatives (need PDI merge before code merge) but no longer have the benefits of it (type safety, automated unpacking, ect).


> If you want to require folks migrating code to fully convert it to PDI 

No, this is not what I asked.  I asked for ONE example of a repo that is improved by this existing.  Nowhere did I ask you to fully convert anything to PDI.

> testing might not be possible.

I'm not sure why you say that.  I routinely accept commits where testing truly isn't possible.  The problem tends to be that people _could_ test at least in partial, or at least review that behavior shouldn't change, but don't want to do the it.

> If you want to ensure that some enum member you are comparing actually exists, this patch can help with that.

It's statements like this that I don't understand without an example.  Very likely as stated this could be an improvement.  I don't really understand it, because PDI already has a first class enum.

> It's to patch up existing code 

And this is where I'm stuck.  You claim to watch to patch up existing code, but can't show an example of existing code that is improved by this.
Continue to not be in support of this.
